content.title: Goals and Highlights for Netherlands 2-1 Norway in Friendly Match
content.text: EVENT ENDEDThe Netherlands came from behind to beat Norway at home in this friendly match in preparation for the World Cup.By Victor CunhaPublished March 27, 2026 – Updated March 27, 2026, 4:39 pm EDTAnd that's all for now! Thank you so much for watching this friendly match, with all the action and excitement in real time here on VAVEL! Stay tuned for updates and upcoming games. Good morning and see you next time! In the first half, Norway took the lead with a goal from Schjelderup, while Van Dijk equalized before halftime. Early in the second half, Reijnders put the Netherlands ahead, sealing a 2-1 victory for the home side! Koopmeiners received the pass at the edge of the area, where he took a powerful long-range shot, sending the ball into Nyland's hands, who didn't give up a rebound. And we'll have two more minutes of added time in this final stretch of the second half at the Johan Cruijff Arena. The Netherlands made further changes, with Gakpo, Gravenberch and Jean Paul van Hecke being replaced by Stefan De Vrij, Jerdy Schouten and Woul Weghorst. Shortly afterwards, from a Xavi Simons cross, De Vrij got a header, but Nyland palmed the ball away. Norway made a change at that moment, with Torbjorn Heggem coming off for Frederik Bjorkan. Shortly after, from a Hauge cross, Larsen managed to turn and shoot, but Verburggen made a startled save in the game! Xavi Simons, who had just come on, received the ball up front and shot hard, but it hit the defense, winning a corner. Koopmeiners took the corner into the box, and Brobbey headed it, but sent the ball wide to the right of the goal. Now it was the Netherlands' turn to make three changes, with Donyell Malen, Tijani Reijnders and Kees Smit leaving and Brian Brobbey, Xavi Simons and Quinten Timber entering. The Netherlands continue to dominate the match, in a second half in which they have conceded very little. Norway made many changes at the moment, with five substitutions, where Moller Wolfe, Schjeldrup, Patrick Berg and Oscar Bobb left, and Kristian Thorstvedt, Felix Myhre, Jens Hauge, Antonio Nusa and Leo Ostigaard entered. The Netherlands continues to dominate the match, exchanging passes and controlling the game, switching possession in the attacking half and managing to create danger for the Norwegian defense, which is no longer able to launch counter-attacks as it did in the first half. Gravenberch received the pass up front, shot hard, and hit the defense. The Netherlands returned dominating the second half, applying pressure in attack and trying to extend their lead, creating constant scoring opportunities. Dumfries, with a good pass inside the area, found Reinjders, who controlled the ball and shot powerfully into the top right corner, putting the Netherlands ahead in the game, now beating Norway, coming from behind at the start of the second half! The players are back on the field and the second half of the match between the Netherlands and Norway is underway, with all the action and excitement in real time here on VAVEL, in this Friday friendly match! In a lively first half, Norway took the lead away from home with a goal from Schjelderup, while the Netherlands equalized through Van Dijk, ending the first half with the game tied 1-1 at the Johan Cruijff Arena! Kees Smit received the pass at the edge of the box, shooting powerfully from distance, but wide. Shortly after, from a Ryerson cross, he managed a strong header, but sent the ball wide to the right of the goal. And we will have two more minutes of added time. Schjelderup received the pass up front and shot hard, but it hit the defense and went wide, winning a corner kick, which was taken into the box and cleared by the defense. Norway tries again to press in the attacking half, creating further chances. The Netherlands continued to apply high pressure, eventually winning a corner on the left, which Koopmeiners delivered into the box for Van Dijk to powerfully head into the back of the net, equalizing the match for the Netherlands! Gakpo received the pass up front and shot hard, but Nyland palmed the ball away. Then Van de Ven crossed for Malen to deflect, Nyland parried, and Reijnders shot on the rebound, but it was blocked by the defense. Wolfe received the pass and found Schjelderup at the edge of the box, who shot into the left corner, sending the ball into the back of the net and opening the scoring for Norway away from home with a beautiful goal for the visiting team! Both teams manage good attacks in the final third, creating danger. The Netherlands maintain possession, controlling the action, while Norway looks for counter-attacks, clearly reflecting what is happening on the pitch at that moment. Moller Wolfe received the pass up front, shooting from distance, but sending the ball wide to the left of the goal. Mommerfence then received the pass up front and found the ball for Gakpo to shoot powerfully, but it was blocked by the defense. On the right, Norway won a corner, taken into the box but cleared by the defense. Following that, Malen received the pass up front, finding Gakpo in the box, who shot powerfully, but the ball deflected off a defender, resulting in another corner, which was also cleared by the defense. We have a tense start to the game, where both teams are pressing, attacking, and trying to create danger on the counter-attack. Neither team is intimidated by the defense, trying to create chances in a game that has had a hectic start! The players are taking to the pitch and the ball is rolling for the Netherlands vs. Norway match, in these first 45 minutes of the friendly game during this FIFA international break, with all the action and excitement in real time here on VAVEL! And Norway faces a taboo when playing against the Netherlands. This is because in eight encounters, the home team has five wins and three draws, having conceded only two goals in two 1-1 draws. And in 1992, Norway last won at home, by a score of 2-1. Finally, in these 22 matches between the two teams, the Netherlands manages to dominate in terms of goals, with 47 scored, averaging 2.14 per game, while Norway scored 28 goals, averaging 1.27 goals per game. At home, as will be the case in today's match, the Netherlands have hosted Norway 10 times, with six wins, two draws, and two losses. In friendlies, there have also been five matches, with two wins, one draw, and two losses. There have been 22 matches in history between the two teams, with 10 wins for the Netherlands, seven draws, and five wins for Norway. In friendlies, there have also been 12 matches between the two teams, with four wins for each side and four draws. For the next game, Ronald Koeman will have the following names to use during the match against Norway: Justin Bijlow, Mark Flekken, Lutsharel Geertruida, Nathan Aké, Stefan de Vrij, Jorrel Hato, Xavi Simons, Luciano Valente, Jeremie Frimpong, Jerdy Schouten, Quinten Timber, Wout Weghorst, Noa Langa and Brian Brobbey. With a 4-3-3 formation, Norway is lined up for tonight's International Friendly match against the Netherlands with: Nyland, Ryerson, Ajer, Heggem and Wolfe; Bobb, Berge and Berg; Sorloth, Larsen and Schjelderup. With a 4-3-3 formation, the Netherlands are lined up for tonight's International Friendly match against Norway with: Verbruggen, Dumfries, Van Hecke, Van Dijk and Van de Ven; Granvenberch, Reijnders and Smit; Koopmeiners, Malen and Gakpo. Finally, today's match takes place at the Johan Cruijff Arena, also known as the Amsterdam Arena. Home of Ajax, the Arena was inaugurated in 1996 and has a capacity of over 50,000 fans, also hosting matches of the Netherlands National Team, in addition to having hosted matches of UEFA Euro 2000 and 2020. On the other side, Norway will be without Haaland, who is resting and will not play in this 'round', and will take the field with the following possible lineup: Nyland, Ryerson, Ostigard, Ajer and Bjorkan; Bobb, Berg, Berge and Hauge; Strand Larsen and Sorloth. For today's game, the Netherlands will field a near-full-strength team, without the injured Memphis Depay, with the following lineup: Verbruggen, Dumfries, Van Dijk, Van de Vem and Ake; Gravenberch, Schouten, Xavi Simons, Reijnders and Gakpo; Malen. Norway finished in Group I with 24 points, going straight to the World Cup. Italy came in second with 18 points, going to the playoffs. Next was Israel, with 12 points, followed by Estonia with four points, and Moldova with only one, thus completing the qualifying group. In the European World Cup qualifiers, the Netherlands led Group G with 20 points, going straight to the World Cup. Below them, with 17 points, came Poland, going to the playoffs. Below them was Finland with 10 points, five above Malta and seven above Lithuania, closing the group. Norway, for its part, comes with three consecutive victories this season, all in qualifying matches. On October 11th, a 5-0 home win came against Israel, with goals from Khalalli (own goal), Haaland (3) and Nachimias (own goal). On November 13th, a 4-1 home win came against Estonia, with goals from Sorlhoth (2) and Haaland (2), while Saarma scored for Estonia. And on the 16th, a 4-1 away win came against Italy, with goals from Nusa, Haaland (2) and Larsen, while Esposito scored for Italy. The Netherlands come into today's game with two wins and a draw in their last matches. On October 12th, they won 4-0 at home against Finland, with goals from Malen, Van Dijk, Depay, and Gakpo. On November 14th, they drew 1-1 with Poland away from home, with Kaminski opening the scoring and Depay equalizing. And on the 17th, they won 4-0 at home against Lithuania, with goals from Reijnders, Gakpo, Zavi Simons, and Malen, all in World Cup qualifying matches. Netherlands vs Norway live face off this Friday (27), at the Johan Cruijff Arena, at 3:45 pm ET, in a Friendly match.
